author: WP19
summary: Appendix giving claim labels, evidence forms, oracle authority by question, the complete evidence vector, automation at the pin, a repair backlog and a minimum claim recipe. The foundations evidence page already defined a vocabulary and a vector; the evidence-form, authority and record tables with CNA instances, the automation facts and the recipe are new on the verification-tiers reference (with the vector figure recreated). The Android coverage, the FNA-first behaviour rule and the C ABI gate details were corrected; the backlog rows are handed to Known Issues.

sections.heading: Oracle authority depends on the question
Renderer and platform claims need a complete vector

concepts.text: A claim-decoding key: tests are not ranked on one weak-to-strong line, because compile probes, hostile-input tests, pixel comparisons and native-host runs answer different questions; the useful record is an evidence vector naming subject, environment, observation point, oracle, result and artifact.
tokens: It does not rank tests on one line from weak to strong

concepts.text: The claim labels describe what was established and are not interchangeable synonyms for "supported".
tokens: The labels describe what was established

concepts.text: Source-proven means a pinned implementation, fallback, refusal or absence was inspected along a reachable route; compile-proven means the declarations, includes, templates and link closure compiled in a recorded configuration.

target.evidence: definition; mapped to the site scale (source exists; configures/builds/links)

concepts.text: Runtime-observed means the named path executed and yielded a recorded state, value, file, trace or lifecycle event; renderer-engaged means the intended family and its native or translation API were identified during execution.

Oracle-compared means an observation was compared with an identified authority under a stated policy; pixel-verified means selected pixels or a frame were compared at a named readback boundary, renderer, host and tolerance.
Manually observed means a person inspected output without a retained discriminating oracle; historically recorded means a dated artifact reports the result but it was not rerun for the claim.
Blocked (an external precondition stopped the route), unsupported (an explicit refusal, absent factory or documented lack) and not attempted (no execution claim) are three different outcomes.

Header or compile probe: establishes that names, signatures, templates, includes and link closure are usable in the selected build, not runtime semantics, resource creation, rendering or host engagement.
Strict-XNA positive probe: code restricted to the intended XNA surface compiles with CNA_STRICT_XNA_API; it does not show the negative guard catches a leak.
Strict-XNA negative probe: a deliberate CNAEXT call fails compilation, proving the guard is sensitive, without proving that every unmarked or misclassified declaration is covered.
Pure deterministic test: a value, transition, parser result or exception matches its asserted oracle on that host, with no renderer, window-system, driver or external-runtime engagement.
Hostile-input test: a named malformed boundary rejects, contains or reports the input as asserted, saying nothing about valid data or the completeness of the malformed corpus.
Trace or HEADLESS test: routing, validation, counters or state order reached the trace implementation, not rasterisation, GPU work, visible pixels or real occlusion samples.
Source-path audit: at the pinned revision a reachable implementation, refusal, fallback or parameter loss is visible in source; it proves neither compilation nor execution on a required host.

Readback or small-pixel test: the exercised renderer produced the asserted value at the selected readback boundary; it says nothing about whole-scene fidelity, another renderer or paths the readback bypasses.
Golden-image comparison: a captured frame matches a retained reference under the recorded tolerance and environment, not that the reference is authoritative or portable.
Differential run: CNA agrees with a named independent implementation or real XNA for the exercised inputs and observation, not general parity; two implementations can share a defect.
Native-host artifact: the requested executable, runtime, device or browser and observation point all engaged on the named host, not on other hosts, identities or long durations.

CI workflow success: the trigger reached every recorded step and its gates passed for that matrix leg; it says nothing about filtered-out jobs, dispatch-only workflows, dead configure legs or tests never registered in that configuration.

"Test exists", "registered", "ran" and "oracle discriminated" are four separate statements: a skip is not a pass, a dry-run mutation is not a killed mutation, and an uploaded log counts only if it identifies binary, configuration, host and observation.

concepts.section: Oracle authority depends on the question
concepts.text: For API shape CNA takes Microsoft's XNA reference assemblies and XML documentation as the target surface; a converted, searchable documentation corpus is a reading aid, not a live gate or a substitute for the original assemblies.
tokens: a converted, searchable copy of that documentation is a reading aid, not a gate

target.evidence: tools/audit_xna_runtime_surface.py (census inputs: Microsoft XML + DLL metadata)

concepts.section: Oracle authority depends on the question
concepts.text: For behaviour the unit says CNA's checklist names FNA as the ordinary reference: corrected, CNA's contributor rules keep FNA as the day-to-day reference but make measured XNA the tie-break (owner decision of 2026-09-04), while a specification or renderer API can outrank both; a project-authored expected value is an oracle only when its derivation is reviewable and independent of the code under test.
tokens: independent of the code under test

target.evidence: CLAUDE.md ("Where FNA and XNA disagree, XNA wins"); CHECKLIST.md still says FNA wins (Known Issues NEW-B6-08)

concepts.section: Oracle authority depends on the question
concepts.text: Public API shape: XNA reference assembly and documentation, C#-to-C++ idioms normalised explicitly, then positive and negative compile probes.

concepts.section: Oracle authority depends on the question
concepts.text: Managed behaviour: real XNA where executable, otherwise pinned FNA plus independently chosen edge cases and documented deliberate deviations.

concepts.section: Oracle authority depends on the question
concepts.text: File-format semantics: the owning specification and independently generated fixtures, with production output compared against a separate decoder or digest where practical.

concepts.section: Oracle authority depends on the question
concepts.text: GPU or API behaviour: the native API contract plus renderer-owned execution evidence, with another renderer used only as a localisation control, never as the sole truth source.

concepts.section: Oracle authority depends on the question
concepts.text: Project extension: a written CNA contract, negative cases and a discriminating test, since XNA and FNA cannot define semantics for a CNA-only feature.

concepts.section: Oracle authority depends on the question
concepts.text: Historical reconstruction: original executables, source, data and versioned captures; decompiled code is evidence to audit, not automatically a behavioural specification.

target.evidence: tools/xna-oracle/reference; test comments citing decompiled XNA sources

concepts.section: Renderer and platform claims need a complete vector
concepts.text: A renderer result records source identity (CNA and sibling commits, local diff, generated tables) and build identity (public selector, family or profile, build type, toolchain, options, exact commands).

concepts.section: Renderer and platform claims need a complete vector
concepts.text: It records host identity (OS and architecture, native or translation runtime, device and driver, display mode, browser or emulator or hardware, environment) and the exact subject (test, demo, asset, API operation, malformed case or route).

concepts.section: Renderer and platform claims need a complete vector
concepts.text: It records engagement proof: a log marker, API or device identity, browser verdict, screenshot, readback or lifecycle trace showing the intended path, not a substitute, ran.

concepts.section: Renderer and platform claims need a complete vector
concepts.text: It records the oracle (expected value, image or exception, authority, tolerance, normalisation), an outcome from pass, fail, expected fail, skip, unsupported, blocked or not attempted rather than one overloaded supported bit, and a retained artifact with a reproducible locator.

concepts.section: Renderer and platform claims need a complete vector
concepts.text: The vector distinguishes a MinGW binary through Wine and DXVK from a native MSVC Direct3D run, an HTTP-served page from a local file, an APK that presents a frame from an Android source path, and an iOS source path from a signed device build; at TARGET no workflow builds Android and the Apple workflow launches a simulator and final-links a device build without running on hardware.
tokens: from a signed build on a physical device

concepts.text: TARGET has 20 workflow files; 18 have an automatic trigger in addition to manual dispatch and the Direct3D and GDI workflows are manual-only.

Claim that the matrix spans Linux, Windows, Web, Android and Apple: corrected, no workflow builds Android, native Wayland, the C API library or the XNA oracle corpus, or enables Diagnostics above OFF or the Inspector.
tokens: Android, native Wayland, a build of the C API library

concepts.text: The workflow breadth is source-proven configuration, not a record that every job passed at TARGET.
tokens: They are source-verified configuration, not a record that any job passed

concepts.text: The C ABI shows why: the unit claims extensive build evidence and a regenerated gate with two unmet criteria; at TARGET no workflow builds the library, the checked-in gate reads "Not ready" with one unmet criterion (468 unmapped symbols) and the coverage generator refuses the unclassified modules, so neither files nor a green subset can promote it to release-ready.
Browser harnesses, sanitizers, mutation routes and native-platform jobs establish only the exact configurations and artifacts they execute.
tokens: establish only the configurations and artifacts they execute

concepts.text: The ledger is presented as a repair backlog: "source-proven" means the defective condition is mechanically visible at the pin, not that a reproducer ran, and each fix should add the discriminating regression named for it.

concepts.text: Before writing "works", answer six questions: which subject and revision, which build/renderer/platform/host engaged, where behaviour was observed, which independent authority supplied the expectation, which negative or perturbed case shows the check can fail, and which artifact lets the next reader reproduce or falsify the claim.
tokens: Which negative or perturbed case shows the check can fail?

concepts.text: A claim that cannot answer all six is labelled with the strongest label it earns and is never silently promoted to behavioural parity.
tokens: do not silently promote it to behavioural parity
